note: Issue 368, governor sheet: the Author's ruling on a governor's low loyalty. His unilateral act is turning toward rebellion; the Diplomat writes, and the PC answers with the one policy that buys a governor back (the-diplomat.md section 7). This is the Diplomat's own town; a seditious governor elsewhere needs a colony-wide condition, on the audit's issue list. The monthly cost is a placeholder. Placeholder prose.

body.text: You should know that {param:governor} is not the Crown's man any longer, whatever he writes to you.

He has not said so. He has put the men to the walls and the powder store, and he is laying in grain beyond what {param:town} will eat, and he has stopped asking after you at table. I have dined with him often enough to know what that means.
It is not too late. He is proud rather than lost, and a proud man can be brought round by being made much of. I could see to that, at {param:cost} a month for his table and mine.

options.text: and wish I had heard it sooner

options.label: cultivate him, at the Crown's charge
options.text: Make much of him, at the Crown's charge. Whatever it costs, it is cheaper than the other thing.

options.label: cultivate him, and bear half yourself
options.text: Make much of him. The Crown will bear half of it; I must ask you to find the rest.

options.label: cultivate him, at your own charge
options.text: Make much of him, and forgive me that the Crown can send nothing towards it.
